task: Implement ML-DSA (FIPS 204) — the Dilithium-based module-lattice signature scheme — from scratch in crypto-core/mldsa.mjs, with a from-scratch property-based test suite, no reference crypto library, no reference test vectors.

entries.description: Read crypto-core/keccak.mjs (SHAKE dependency), crypto-core/mlkem.mjs (house style for lattice crypto: NTT patterns, sampling, encoding), crypto-core/mlkem.test.mjs (verification standard), cli/proofbundle-cli.mjs (seal/verify/keygen CLI semantics), and the mlkem_scaffold_agent_* provenance files as a template.
entries.result: Confirmed hash primitives come only from keccak.mjs (shake128/shake256/sha3_256/sha3_512); confirmed sealCore/verifyCore require the worklog to be a JSON object, not an array, and rejects arrays with MALFORMED.

entries.description: Cross-checked FIPS 204 Table 1/2 parameters and byte-size formulas by hand and numerically (node) before writing code: bit-widths for t1 (10), t0 (13=d), s1/s2 (3 for eta=2, 4 for eta=4), z (18 for gamma1=2^17, 20 for gamma1=2^19), and w1 (6 for gamma2=(q-1)/88, 4 for gamma2=(q-1)/32); verified these reproduce the exact FIPS 204 pk/sk/sig sizes for all three parameter sets (44: 1312/2560/2420, 65: 1952/4032/3309, 87: 2592/4896/4627) via arithmetic before implementation.
entries.result: All derived bit-widths matched the target sizes exactly, confirming the encoding scheme before any code was written.

entries.description: Computed in node (BigInt modpow) that 1753^512 mod 8380417 == 1 and 1753^256 mod 8380417 == q-1 (i.e. -1), confirming 1753 has multiplicative order exactly 512 mod q — the precondition for a full 8-layer/256-point NTT (X^256+1 splits into 256 linear factors since q ≡ 1 mod 512).
entries.result: Confirmed zeta=1753 is valid; proceeded to implement a full NTT (unlike ML-KEM's 7-layer incomplete NTT) with plain coordinatewise multiplication in the transformed domain.

entries.description: Implemented ML-DSA-44/65/87 from scratch: modular arithmetic (mod, mod±, powMod, bitlen); full 8-layer NTT and inverse NTT mod 8380417 derived from bit-reversed powers of zeta=1753 (not a transcribed table); coordinatewise NTT-domain multiplication; schoolbook multiplication exported for independent verification; Power2Round; Decompose/HighBits/LowBits with the q-1 boundary special case; MakeHint/UseHint; SimpleBitPack/BitPack signed packing at multiple bit widths; hint run-length encode/decode; ExpandA (SHAKE128 rejection sampling of 23-bit candidates, mirroring ML-KEM's sampleNTT structure); ExpandS (SHAKE256 rejection sampling for eta=2 and eta=4 bounded coefficients); ExpandMask (direct SHAKE256 bit-unpack, no rejection needed since 2*gamma1 is a power of 2); SampleInBall (Fisher-Yates shuffle over SHAKE256 output); pkEncode/skEncode/sigEncode and inverses with explicit length validation; the KeyGen/Sign/Verify internal algorithms and the rejection-sampling sign loop; and the public API mldsaKeygen/mldsaSign/mldsaVerify, fully deterministic (all randomness — seed32, rnd32 — supplied by the caller, nothing reaches for ambient entropy). Imports only shake128/shake256 from ./keccak.mjs; no cryptographic library of any kind.

Before writing the full test suite, ran ad hoc node scripts to check NTT round-trip (3 seeds), NTT-multiplication vs schoolbook (2 seeds), Power2Round round-trip (20 random values, exact equality), and Decompose round-trip including the q-1 boundary case (mod-q equality) for both gamma2 values.
entries.result: All primitives correct on first implementation attempt — no NTT sign/index bugs.

entries.description: Ran ad hoc node scripts exercising mldsaKeygen/mldsaSign/mldsaVerify for all three parameter sets: checked pk/sk/sig byte lengths against the FIPS 204 tables and checked sign-then-verify succeeds.
entries.result: ML-DSA-44 pk=1312 sk=2560 sig=2420 (all exact matches), verify=true, ~0.29s. ML-DSA-65 pk=1952 sk=4032 sig=3309 (exact), verify=true, ~0.46s. ML-DSA-87 pk=2592 sk=4896 sig=4627 (exact), verify=true, ~0.74s. Correct on first attempt for all three parameter sets.

entries.description: Wrote the from-scratch property-based test suite in the mlkem.test.mjs style: NTT invertibility (4 seeds); NTT-domain multiplication vs an independently computed schoolbook convolution mod (X^256+1) (3 seeds); Power2Round round-trip (exact integer reconstruction, ~208 samples including boundary values); Decompose round-trip (mod-q reconstruction, ~207 samples per gamma2 including the q-1 special case, for both gamma2 values used across the parameter sets); and for each of ML-DSA-44/65/87: pk/sk/sig size conformance, sign/verify agreement, sign determinism (same key+rnd -> byte-identical signature), distinct-rnd -> distinct-but-valid signature, and five independent rejection checks (flipped signature bit inside z, flipped cTilde bit, flipped message bit, signature verified under a different public key, a different key's signature rejected against this key, truncated signature, and overlong/padded signature).

entries.result: 51 pass, 0 fail on first run of the complete suite. Repeated 3 additional times to rule out flakiness from the Math.random() round-trip sampling in the Power2Round/Decompose tests: 51 pass, 0 fail every time.

entries.description: Ran the other crypto-core suites (keccak.test.mjs, mlkem.test.mjs, sha256.test.mjs) to confirm no shared file was touched and nothing else regressed. Grepped mldsa.mjs for noble/webcrypto/node:crypto imports.
entries.result: keccak: 102 pass 0 fail. mlkem: 35 pass 0 fail. sha256: 5 pass 0 fail. No forbidden imports found in mldsa.mjs — only './keccak.mjs' (shake128, shake256) is imported.

entries.description: Additional ad hoc checks beyond the required test list: empty message sign/verify, plain-string message (auto UTF-8 encoded) vs Uint8Array message mismatch correctly rejected, 100000-byte message sign/verify, and verifying a signature against the wrong parameter-set name (fails closed with false, does not throw).
